Basing a very long and argumentative paragraph on a flimsy and arbitrary definition. Good job. Any amount of senseless comparisons can't help you assert that there is anything particularly troubling going on. The desecration of a term that never had any essence to begin with is hardly a tragedy.

Now in essence you're right of course, some (many ?) big name RPGs have gone to shit. Every game with stats is called an RPG (e.g. Borderlands), and games that we call RPGs have largely lost the role-playing part. Even the better games that we call RPGs are not really doing much in the way of role playing.

But that's the thing though, actual role-playing is an incredibly niche entertainment form. When I play videogame RPGs these days, I care about the depth of tactical combat in Dragon Age: Origins, I care about the writing in The Witcher 3. And make no mistake, I also enjoy a non-linear story, however not because I want to role-play but because I want to explore a chain of events dependent on the choices I make, much like I like exploring Minecraft worlds just for the sake of exploration.

And in effect, the removal of permanent choices helps MMOs such as Guild Wars 2 tremendously when it comes to bringing people to the core gameplay as fast and annoyance-free as possible. Nobody designed that system with role-playing in mind. Maybe you feel betrayed by such a design choice, but that's the extent of the crime. MMORPGs have been studied somewhat extensively, the largest and most profitable players are those that play to reach goals, get gratification and amass power. It's a bit trivial, but it works and those are the players being catered to the most. Then comes those that seek to excel in whatever it is that is the core gameplay, preferably something competitive, those are the ones who will play the meta and make it evolve. What I'm getting at is that the role-playing features of MMOs have been gradually faded out as everybody realized few players (i.e. those not in that "part of the MMORPG community") actually cared about them. Exact same thing happened to solo RPGs. This drift is not responsible for the amount of "RPGs" that are simply bad games as those would have been bad games even if they followed your principles of what is an RPG.

And overall I think it has been a good transition. Tab-target monster farm mash-your-skill-buttons is shit gameplay anyway, the noble art of role-playing deserves a better platform. Honestly, the best roleplaying I've ever did in video-games was playing an obscure multiplayer mod for the obscure turkish medieval combat game Mount & Blade Warband. The extent of my roleplaying was adhering to a strict disciple in equipment choice (being naked) that actually meant something because 1) I was the only one doing it 2) Tight knit community would mean most of everyone was instantly recognizable, especially me sticking out 3) That was a severe disadvantage that I could handle because I was fucking good (yes that's bragging). MMOs are quite simply a bad setup for this. I see little sense in role-playing with complete strangers I will never "meet" again. Even in that game with merely a face editor plus rudimentary equipment and stat choices I could do more meaningful role-playing than in all MMOs I played combined.
Maybe you should broaden your horizons. There's plenty of innovative content out there, it's just not as traditional as you would like.
